chunks: And by his chain, he said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: “O group of the poor ones, be of good heart, and give Allah contentment from your hearts. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will reward you for your poverty. But if you do not do so, then there is no reward for you.”

key_terms.الرِّضَا: contentment and willing acceptance for the sake of Allah
key_terms.الْمَسَاكِينِ: the poor and needy people being addressed by the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.ثَوَابَ: reward from Allah for one’s response and spiritual state
key_terms.طِيبُوا: be comforted and maintain a good and settled state
key_terms.فَقْرِكُمْ: your poverty and state of material hardship
key_terms.قُلُوبِكُمْ: your hearts, meaning inward sincerity and inner state

ai.seo_question: Does Islam say that poverty itself is rewarded, or only patience and contentment in poverty?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the poor believers to meet poverty with inward contentment and sincere acceptance for the sake of Allah. It emphasizes that reward is tied not merely to being poor, but to responding with heartfelt riḍā and steadiness before Allah.
